questions.question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A with column-B?

Column-A (Name of Vitamin) Column-B (Deficiency Diseases)

i. Vitamin A a. Scurvy

ii. Vitamin D b. Beriberi

iii. Vitamin B1 c. Rickets

iv. Vitamin C d. Night Blindness
questions.option_1: i - d, ii - c, iii - b, iv - a
questions.option_2: i - a, ii - c, iii - d, iv - b
questions.option_3: i - d, ii - a, iii - c, iv - b
questions.option_4: i - b, ii - d, iii - a, iv - c
questions.solution:
The correct matches for vitamins and their deficiency diseases are:
  • i-d: Vitamin A deficiency causes Night Blindness.
  • ii-c: Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets.
  • iii-b: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beriberi.
  • iv-a: Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy.

questions.question: Vitamin D is synthesised using sunshine, by the:
questions.solution:
Vitamin D is uniquely synthesized by the skin when it is exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) rays from sunlight.
  • This process converts cholesterol in the skin into Vitamin D3, which is then further processed by the liver and kidneys to become active.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
questions.solution:
Goitre is a mineral deficiency disease caused by a lack of Iodine in the diet.
  • Iodine is essential for the thyroid gland to produce hormones; without it, the gland enlarges, causing a swelling in the neck.
  • Note: Scurvy and Rickets are vitamin deficiencies, and Marasmus is a protein-energy malnutrition.

questions.question: The digestive enzymes inside lysosomes are made by:
questions.solution:
The digestive enzymes found inside lysosomes are synthesized by the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER).
  • These enzymes are then transported to the Golgi apparatus, where they are packaged into the vesicles that become lysosomes.

questions.question: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
questions.solution:
Whales belong to the class Mammalia.
  • Despite their fish-like appearance and aquatic habitat, whales are warm-blooded, breathe air through lungs, and give birth to live young that they nurse with milk.

questions.question: Which of the following phyla contains Leech?
questions.solution:
Leeches belong to the phylum Annelida.
  • Annelids are characterized by segmented bodies. Leeches belong specifically to the class Hirudinea and are often external parasites (ectoparasites).

questions.question: Which of the following options is an example of a decomposer in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
In an ecosystem, Fungus (along with bacteria) is a primary example of a decomposer.
  • Decomposers break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients back into the soil for producers (plants) to use.

questions.question: National Prophylaxis Program, which was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to address which of the following medical conditions /diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies?
questions.solution:
The National Prophylaxis Program against Nutritional Blindness was launched to address Vitamin A deficiency in children.
  • The program distributes high-dose Vitamin A supplements to prevent Xerophthalmia and associated blindness.

questions.question: According to sympatric speciation, the rising of a new species occurs when:
questions.option_1: two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location
questions.option_2: the two groups of organisms from the same species would phenotypically look different
questions.option_3: organisms from the same species start to show different behavioural characteristics
questions.option_4: one species is separated into different groups due to geologic events like mountain formation
questions.solution:
Sympatric speciation occurs when a new species evolves from a surviving ancestral species while both continue to inhabit the same geographic location.
  • This usually happens through reproductive isolation, where two groups stop interbreeding due to genetic or behavioral changes, despite no physical barrier being present.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is detected by the Widal test?
questions.solution:
The Widal test is a serological test used for the diagnosis of Typhoid fever.
  • It detects the presence of specific antibodies against the Salmonella typhi bacteria in a patient's serum.

questions.question:
If after being bitten by a mosquito, the person is detected as being malaria positive, which of the following will hold true?

A. The person did not have a balanced diet.

B. The mosquito was carrying plasmodium.

C. The mosquito was suffering from malaria.

D. The person was not vaccinated as a child.
questions.solution:
If a person tests positive for malaria, it means the mosquito was carrying Plasmodium.
  • Malaria is caused by the protozoan parasite Plasmodium, which is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

questions.question:
Match the columns.

Column A (Plant Group) Column B (Example)

i. Bryophyta a. Rose

ii. Pteridophyta b. Pine

iii. Gymnosperms c. Mosses

iv. Angiosperms d. Selaginella
questions.option_1: i - c, ii - d, iii - b, iv - a
questions.option_2: i - b, ii - c, iii - a, iv - d
questions.option_3: i - d, ii - b, iii - c, iv - a
questions.option_4: i - a, ii - d, iii - b, iv - c
questions.solution:
The correct matches for plant groups and examples are:
  • i-c: Bryophyta includes Mosses.
  • ii-d: Pteridophyta includes Selaginella (and ferns).
  • iii-b: Gymnosperms include Pine.
  • iv-a: Angiosperms include Rose (flowering plants).

questions.question: What is the primary function of the notochord in chordates?
questions.solution:
The primary function of the notochord in chordates is to provide skeletal support.
  • It is a flexible, rod-like structure that runs along the back, serving as an axis for muscle attachment and maintaining the body's shape.

questions.question: By what name is the species of Scaphopoda Mollusca 'Dentalium' commonly known?
questions.solution:
Dentalium, a member of the class Scaphopoda, is commonly known as Tusk shells or Tooth shells.
  • These mollusks have a tubular shell that is open at both ends and shaped like an elephant's tusk.

questions.question: Stunted growth, which is common in children growing up in extreme poverty, is a sure sign of ____________.
questions.solution:
Stunted growth in children is a clinical sign of chronic undernutrition.
  • It occurs when a child does not receive adequate nutrients or suffers from repeated infections over a long period, preventing them from reaching their full growth potential.

questions.question: What is the study of the interactions between living organisms and their environment called?
questions.solution:
Ecology is the branch of biology that deals with the interactions between living organisms and their physical environment.
  • It studies how organisms affect and are affected by both biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) factors.

questions.question: Which virus is responsible for causing common cold?
questions.solution:
The Rhinovirus is the most common viral infectious agent in humans and is the primary cause of the common cold.
  • Note: Influenza causes the flu, which is generally more severe than a cold.

questions.question: Based on the number of chambers in the heart, select the odd one from the following.
questions.solution:
The Crocodile is the odd one out because it has a four-chambered heart.
  • Chameleons, Frogs, and Turtles generally have a three-chambered heart. Crocodiles are unique among reptiles for having a heart structure similar to birds and mammals.

questions.question: Which virus is responsible for causing AIDS?
questions.solution:
The virus responsible for causing AIDS is the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).
  • HIV attacks the body's immune system, specifically the CD4 cells (T cells), making the individual susceptible to opportunistic infections.

questions.question:
Find the odd one out.

Vacuoles, Nucleus, Ribosomes, Lysosomes
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are the odd one out because they are non-membrane-bound organelles.
  • Vacuoles, the Nucleus, and Lysosomes are all bound by membranes.

questions.question: In animal cells, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids through ꞵ-oxidation is conducted by which of the following organelles?
questions.solution:
In animal cells, while most fatty acid oxidation occurs in mitochondria, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids (VLCFA) is initiated in Peroxisomes.
  • This process shortens the chains so they can eventually be fully oxidized in the mitochondria.

questions.question: When protein-rich gelatinous egg white is heated, it turns to solid white due to:
questions.solution:
The transformation of egg white from a clear liquid to an opaque solid when heated is due to protein denaturation.
  • Heat breaks the weak chemical bonds that hold the protein (albumin) in its folded shape, causing it to uncoil and then clump together (coagulate) into a solid mass.
